operators.name: custom_sum_dim

parameters.name: x
parameters.shape: [B, C, H, W] where in this task B=512, C=3, H=512, W=512
parameters.layout: supports strides; may be non-contiguous? reference input is contiguous in task but op should handle strided tensors if provided

returns.shape: [B, H, W] (sum over dimension dim, which is self.in_channels; in this task dim=1, so output 512x512x512)

semantics: Computes torch.sum(x, dim=dim) exactly, preserving kahan-like behavior? Reference uses standard PyTorch sum; our CUDA implementation should match within tolerance
Input x is a 4D tensor [B, C, H, W]; sum over the specified dimension, reducing it; output is 3D [B, H, W] if dim=1 (general output shape removes the dim-th dimension)
No keepdim, so dimension is squeezed
Must handle arbitrary strides, but for performance can use contiguous path as reference input is contiguous
Output tensor allocated with same dtype and device (CUDA)
